label: Sovereignty (Magical/Legal)
notes: Dumézil I: Represents cosmic/legal order, sacred authority, knowledge, magic (e.g., Odin, Varuna)

label: Sovereignty (Priestly/Juridical)
notes: Dumézil I: Represents justice, contracts, ritual leadership (e.g., Mitra, Tyr as law-giver)

label: Warrior Function
notes: Dumézil II: Represents physical force, protection, courage, martial prowess (e.g., Thor, Indra)

label: Fertility/Prosperity Function
notes: Dumézil III: Represents fecundity, nourishment, health, wealth, peace (e.g., Freyja, Ashvins)

label: Trickster/Mediator
notes: Boundary-crosser, agent of change, subverter of order, often a cultural catalyst; Jakobsonian

label: Civilizer/Culture Hero
notes: Brings foundational elements of culture like fire, agriculture, arts, laws; Jakobsonian

label: Cosmic Orderer
notes: Deity/force responsible for establishing or maintaining cosmic laws and structures

label: Destroyer/Transformer
notes: Deity/force embodying destruction necessary for transformation or renewal (e.g., Shiva, Kali)

label: Healer Function
notes: Deity/hero associated with curing illness, restoring health, and alleviating suffering

label: Psychopomp (Soul Guide)
notes: Guides souls of the deceased to the afterlife

label: Oracle/Prophet Function
notes: Character or force that reveals divine will, hidden knowledge, or future events

label: Guardian/Protector
notes: Role of protecting specific places, people, thresholds, or principles

label: Creator/Demiurge
notes: Primary agent responsible for the creation of the cosmos or aspects thereof

label: Antagonist/Obstructer
notes: Force or character that opposes the protagonist or cosmic order, creating conflict
